dame.1: A free app with nobody's name on it. In my experience, Shieldy, when you can't see who is selling, you are what's being sold.
dame.2: Sprout trusts easily. That isn't a fault. It's the thing we are here to protect.
dame.3: Notice how quiet the children have gone. A city full of secrets is a city where somebody is collecting them.
dame.4: When you speak to someone who was tricked, your first sentence decides whether they ever tell anyone again.
dame.5: We don't win by being cleverer than Glitch. We win when nobody is left alone with him.
dame.6: Rest, Knight. Tomorrow we write to the other cities.

pixel.1: I looked up who registered ShineUp. The address is a car park. A CAR PARK, Shieldy.
pixel.2: A profile picture takes four seconds to steal. I timed it.
pixel.3: I can trace a van. I can't trace why a kid would rather talk to a stranger than to us. That part is on us.
pixel.4: I keep thinking about that sticker. I was so ready to be angry with Nova. I'm glad Dame Noble slowed me down.
pixel.5: Two hundred and twelve screenshots. Evidence is just the truth with a date on it.
pixel.6: I'm writing a guide: "How to check an app before you join." Page one: find out who made it.

bot.1: I do not understand sparks. They are numbers. I already have many numbers.
bot.2: QUERY: if a friend will not show their face, is it a friend, or a username? I do not have enough data.
bot.3: I shared my password to prove friendship. This was an error. Friendship does not require a password.
bot.4: I wanted to hide what happened to my account. Hiding used more energy than telling. I am a very efficient robot now.
bot.5: STATUS: two-step login ON. Location OFF. Profile PRIVATE. Feelings: GOOD.
bot.6: The drones named Kevin have been recycled into a toaster. It is a good toaster.

sprout.1: Everyone in my class has ShineUp! I've got 200 sparks already. Is that a lot? It feels like a lot.
sprout.2: StarKnight said I was his best friend. Was any of it true? Even a little bit?
sprout.3: Milo's gone all quiet. He used to tell me everything. Now he says it's "private".
sprout.4: Is Nova bad? …No. I don't think so. I think she was scared, like me, but for much longer.
sprout.5: I told my whole class about the code word. Seven of them have one now!
sprout.6: I still post photos. Just not ones with my school or my house in them. Biscuit is allowed, but only her face.

nova.1: Free sparks, everybody! …Sorry, Knight, can't talk. I'm live. I'm always live.
nova.2: You're still looking into ShineUp? Why? It's just an app. Honestly. Leave it.
nova.3: I didn't sleep. It's nothing. Streamers never sleep. Please stop looking at me like that.
nova.4: I keep waiting for someone to shout at me. Nobody has. I don't know what to do with that.
nova.5: I switched my stream off for a week. A whole week. The quiet is strange. I think I like it.
nova.6: I get messages every day now. Kids saying "it happened to me". I answer every one: tell someone. Today.

milo.1: I'm ten levels ahead of Finn on ShineUp. TEN.
milo.2: Luna says I'm the funniest person she's ever met. You wouldn't get it.
milo.3: I can't talk about Luna. It's private. She said so.
milo.4: Gran and I have a deal now. I tell her things, she doesn't freak out. Mostly she doesn't freak out.
milo.5: I'm a detective now. Gran says so. Detectives keep evidence.
milo.6: Luna never even existed. I was sad about that for a while. Is that weird? Gran says it isn't weird.

tess.1: I drew Nova! Do you think she'll see it if I post it on ShineUp?
tess.2: StarKnight wants a photo of me. His camera's broken, so he can't send one back. That's fair, isn't it?
tess.3: I didn't send the photo. I don't know why. It just felt like a tummy ache.
tess.4: Everyone's saying mean things about Nova. I don't want to say any.
tess.5: That tummy-ache feeling was right! Dame Noble says it's called trusting your gut.
tess.6: I draw the Knights now. You're harder to draw than Nova. It's the helmet.

finn.1: I don't really like ShineUp. But if I'm not on it, nobody talks to me at break.
finn.2: AceRider's fifteen and he talks to ME. Nobody that old ever talks to me.
finn.3: Ace got angry when I wouldn't give him my password. Friends don't get angry about that. Do they?
finn.4: If someone had a secret of mine, I think I'd do nearly anything too. That's scary to think about.
finn.5: I told my dad about Ace. He was quiet for a bit, and then he said "thank you for telling me". That was all.
finn.6: Jay's teaching me to skateboard. He's sixteen. And real. I checked.

jay.1: ShineUp? Bit young for me. My little brother's glued to it, though.
jay.2: Some account keeps messaging my brother. Says it's twelve. Types like it's forty.
jay.3: My brother's started locking his door. He's eight. What has an eight-year-old got to hide?
jay.4: People at school are passing round a link to "the Nova video". I haven't opened it. I told two mates not to. One listened.
jay.5: I sat down with my brother last night and we went through his friends list. He deleted nine "friends" he has never met.
jay.6: If a kid asks me for help, I don't say "what did you do?" I say "okay, I'm here". I learned that this year.

rose.1: A purple box on every corner, and nobody asked us. In my day you needed a permit for a flower stall.
rose.2: Milo is always on that telephone, smiling at it. I'm glad he has friends. I do wonder who they are.
rose.3: He doesn't chat at dinner any more. Something has hold of that boy, and it isn't homework.
rose.4: I told Milo my secret about the man from the bank. I thought he would think less of me. He hugged me instead.
rose.5: The knitting circle has become the telling circle. Nine grandmothers and a great deal of tea.
rose.6: Come in, dear. There's cake. There is always cake for people who listen.

sam.1: Thirty years on this round and I've never delivered so much nothing. Kiosks, flyers, free this, free that.
sam.2: You see a lot from the pavement. Children walking home with their eyes on their phones, and no idea who is behind them.
sam.3: The little ones have stopped waving at me. They hurry past as if they're late for something.
sam.4: Folk are quick to blame the girl. I've delivered her post since she was six. She's a child, and somebody used her.
sam.5: There's a leaflet in every letterbox on my round now. "Ask them what they're playing. Then listen."
sam.6: It's a quieter round these days. In a good way. More children on bikes.

mum.4: I keep thinking: a whole year, and I didn't notice. Then I think: she can tell me now. That's what matters.
mum.5: The officer said the kindest thing: "You'd be surprised how often it happens. And how well it goes when they tell."
mum.6: We have a new rule at home. No phones at dinner, and no question is ever too embarrassing.

1: My daughter begged for that ShineUp thing. I said yes. Everyone has it, don't they?
Free, they say. I've lived long enough to wonder what free costs.
I couldn't tell you what my son does on his phone. Games, I suppose.
2: My boy has a new friend online. Very polite, apparently. I've never seen so much as a photo.
There was a purple van outside the school again. Deliveries, probably.
She has posted every day of our holiday. The whole street knows we're away.
3: Mine's gone quiet. "Nothing's wrong, Dad." That's all I get.
I asked what she was typing and she turned the phone over. That's new.
When I was young we kept diaries. Now the diary answers back.
4: They're saying that streamer girl brought it on herself. I'm not so sure. She's fifteen.
I asked my son, calmly, whether anyone had ever asked him for a photo. He went white. We talked all evening.
If mine were in trouble, would she tell me? I'd like to think so. I'm going to make sure.
5: We went through her settings together. It took ten minutes. I should have done it a year ago.
I rang the helpline, just to ask. Nobody judged. They just helped.
My son told me something hard yesterday. I said "thank you for telling me" before I said anything else.
6: It's a different town now. People ask each other things.
No more purple boxes. I don't miss them.
My daughter showed me a strange message this morning, before she had even answered it. That's all I ever wanted.

kids6: I told my mum. She hugged me. I was scared for nothing.
Nova waved at me today! The real Nova, not the stream one.
My friend got a weird message and showed me straight away. We showed her dad together.
I've got a code word, a private profile and two-step login. Try and trick me now.
Postman Sam says I'm the safest kid on his round.
